# Everything we measured and did not get to work: a census of public chains, 111 closed avenues with their conditions, the levers we could not use, and open questions

*Team LordProcciuto. Disclosure: an LLM (Claude) was used for this work. The code of our best submission (e30_a) is public under the MIT license: https://github.com/siming767-creator/whestbench-lordprocciuto*

**How to read.** **x** = ratio of final-layer MSE to a stated reference (<1 is better). **score** = MSE x max(0.1, C/B). **u** = 2^31 FLOPs (one 1024x1024 matmul); B = 1024 u; floor 102.4 u. "nets 0-3" = four official Mini networks with a 1e9-sample truth (local oracles); "70-99" = 30 reserved Mini networks; "server, n pub" = paired comparison on n of the 50 public networks through real submissions. **[M]** measured by us, **[C]** cited from a public source, **[I]** our inference. All as of 14/10/2026.

## 2. Technical context (the minimum needed to read the rest)

- **Task.** 16-layer, width-1024 ReLU MLP with He-initialised Gaussian weights; predict E[h_l(X)] for every layer; graded on the final-layer MSE x max(0.1, C/B), C counted by flopscope; 120 s wall; 0.4 s of Python outside flopscope; 8 GB.
- **Our estimator family (e16 -> e30_a).** Cumulant propagation on the public K=3 line. Mean and full covariance C are propagated with the Gaussian/Edgeworth closure of the ReLU. **Third-order memory κ3 is kept per source**: each layer's "newborn" κ3 is stored with dense legs and carried forward by W and the ReLU slopes. Sources of age 1-4 (*young*) stay dense; sources of age >= 5 are compressed into a shared fixed basis of rank 416/224 (448/224 earlier) - the **"old level"** (root: 504aldo's V29). κ4 is *regenerated* each layer from a scalar law (G = diag + lambda_l.C_off), not stored. A ridge "mean-correction" table (87 features, fitted on 70 nets) removes ~10 % MSE. Neurons with alpha < -2.85 are physically removed. Large products use Strassen (5 levels) with a Winograd leaf. Fixed costs were made exact.
- **Cost/accuracy at the best submission.** Raw final-layer MSE ~2.0e-8 on the public nets (e28fijo, 335741: 1.975e-8 at ~167 u; e30_a trades ~+3 % MSE for ~-6 % FLOPs, so ~158 u [derived]); ~0.15-0.16 B; score 3.12e-9 (the score is the mean over nets of MSE x u/1024, so it is not exactly the product of the two means: 1.975e-8 x 167.5/1024 = 3.23e-9 vs the graded 3.1753e-9 for e28fijo).
- **Terms used below.** D3 = κ3(i,i,i) (a vector per layer). D21 = κ3(i,i,j) (an n x n slice). *Hub* = κ3 with three distinct indices (n^3 numbers). (3,1), (2,2), (2,1,1) = slices of κ4. *Slab* = the correction of D21/(3,1) restricted to the r dominant modes of the pre-activation covariance. *Gap* H = truth - our estimator for the slab. *Born/newborn* = the κ3 created in a layer (age 1).
- **Our graded trajectory** (public ids): 2.438e-8 (01/10, first K=3) -> 4.935e-9 (V29 + dead-neuron removal, 333521) -> 4.017e-9 (+ ridge tables, 333693) -> 3.753e-9 (+ Strassen/rank-1 pieces, 333752) -> 3.61e-9 (clock fixes, 333846) -> 3.591e-9 (e16, 334391) -> 3.5596e-9 (+ Winograd leaf, 334445) -> **3.3072e-9** (fixed-basis old level, 335690) -> 3.2379e-9 (old level only in non-hot rows, 335727) -> 3.1753e-9 (exact fixed-cost savings, 335741) -> **3.1163e-9** (tau 2.85, R_OLD 416, hot 3.0, tilt -0.1; 335981).

No public chain compresses below shared-basis rank 384 at age 4. Forum/Kaggle covariance or sampling notebooks are >= 25x worse.

### 5.2 Aggregate telemetry of the top 10 (public data only; **every attribution is an inference**)

Data: ~2,200 graded submissions with per-network detail; best submission per team as of 13/10. We do not attribute methods to individual teams; the forum rules explicitly allow reusing MIT-licensed public code. In aggregate: today no top-10 error profile is a recognisable copy of any public chain - their profiles sit at "independent-chain" distance (0.072-0.092 by sd of per-net ln-MSE difference; calibration: exact copies <= 0.005, independent chains 0.077 +- 0.008), so the final profile cannot tell a rebuilt public chain from an independent one. Other telemetry [M]:
- **Cost profile per net.** V29's (sd of ln u 1.2 %) correlates 0.04-0.14 with the leaders' (0.29 for one); leaders' cost profiles correlate 0.93-0.99 among themselves (it is simply a function of live neurons, so it does not separate families). Two cost groups: slope ~0.9-1.1 with no fixed block (7 of 10, saving 16-37 u of fixed block vs ours) and slope 0.4-0.7 with a fixed block (30-78 u).
- **Clock is a balance, not a fingerprint.** Mean core clock ~76-80 s almost independent of u (fit 81.3 - 0.027 u s); only the billed-call overhead and residual separate groups (V29-like 2.3-7.6 s / 0.06-0.26 s vs 8.8-12.1 s / 0.32-0.38 s).
- **Depth profile.** No team changed the accumulation law w.r.t. V29: all-layers/last 0.393-0.432 (ours 0.390); one team flatter (exponent 1.50 vs our 1.79).
- **The gain is all-layer and multiplicative per network** (x0.60-0.72 on all layers, x0.57-0.69 on the last, both relative to our e28fijo), which excludes output-only correctors.
- **`setup` FLOPs (not billed in u).** 0 for several teams; 2.8e10, 5.3e10 and 4.2e11 for three (offline precomputation or calibration [I]).
- **Ladder.** One-submission jumps >= 40 % coincide with adopting a public method; the rest is gradual, of two kinds: cost at equal MSE (steps -5..-32 %: fast multiplication, fixed basis) and precision at constant cost (steps -3..-9 %, in clusters of 2-6 separated by 4-10 quiet days). Twelve teams landed at 1.76-1.80e-8 during 23-30/09 with no public cause (the only candidate with a number: a dense κ4 channel, -8.5 % [C]).
- **Where the leaders spend [I].** With the old level removed our estimator is x28-34 worse than e16 on the public nets, whereas leaders at ~110 u keep x0.55-0.66 of e16's MSE: their long memory sits in an object of <~ 10-15 u that is neither our compressed old level at rank 128 (x1.4-1.5), nor the transported basis, nor the hub (x7.3 if removed).

### 5.3 Where the error lives (our estimator, nets 0-3 unless noted)

- **Causal chain.** Final error <- drift of the mean (75-80 % inherited) <- variance of the pre-activations <- off-diagonal covariance C_off of the previous layer (70-78 %) + κ3 iij (19-27 %); κ4 <= 4 % (e16, 08/10). On e24hot (14/10), injecting the true marginal law of every z removes: mean 78.6 %, σ² 41.8 %, κ3-diag 21.2 %, κ4-diag 6.8 %; σ²+κ3+κ4 without the mean 80.4 %; C_off alone 31.2 %.
- **By layer.** Increments born in layers 9..15 are 5.2/9.5/12.4/11.7/14.1/17.5/24.0 % (layers 1-8 ~0; 94 % in 9-15). An error born in layer l is damped ~x0.8 per layer; the output "remembers" 6-7 layers.
- **By term.** 98 % of the σ² error is the *off-diagonal* post covariance of the previous layer (diagonal K2 only 2 %); created by the ReLU step given exact input ~1 %, inherited ~99 %. Of the σ² error^2, true C_off alone removes 71 %, true D21 52 %, true κ4 off-diagonal slices 26 %, the three together 98 %. Closed-loop: D21 alone 15.3 % (layers 9-15) / 21.9 % (1-15), κ4 off slices 9.5 %, D21+κ4 30.8 % (synergy), K2 whole 43 %. D3 (κ3-diag) is *created* at its own formation (~89 %), independent of σ², C_off, D21.
- **By age (corrected 14/10).** D21 relative error by age 10.9/10.3/9.8/9.1/8.5/7.8/7.0/6.2/6.5/6.0/5.6/5.0 % for ages 1-12 (monotone, no jump at the 4/5 boundary); young sources (1-4) hold 71.6 % of the D21 error^2 (relative error 9.21 %), old ones (>= 5) 17.7 % (4.57 %). In MSE: young sources 33.6 % (30.4 % refit), old 7.9 % (6.6 %). *Our earlier statement that the old part had an 8.7 % error and cost ~20 % was an artifact of a weakly identified regression and is withdrawn.* Error at birth is intrinsic (92 %), diffuse (not low-rank, not in the fine legs, not at the ReLU knee) and decays ~x0.8 per age.
- **The birth term.** Of the age-1 error^2, the hub (three distinct indices) is 87-95 %, the iij part 5-13 % (the rank-8 truncation of the residual: rank 256 turns it into 0.6 %), the diagonal 0 %. The hub's Gaussian part is right (error 3.5-4.6 %, cos 0.999); the error is the **non-Gaussian increment** (4.4-4.8 % of hub energy, ~21 % amplitude): 95.6 % (D21) / 97.0 % (D3) of the hub error^2; we reproduce it at cos 0.76 with 0.54 of its amplitude. Split of the increment: odd (κ3, κ5..) 0.64, even (κ4, κ6, κ3^2) 0.36, marginal (all diagonal orders) 0.012; we carry 0.40 of the odd part and none of the even part.
- **Slab oracles.** Exact slab on r=128 modes for κ3 and r=32 for κ4 plus exact D3, g4 (layers 9-15): fraction 0.787 of the ceiling; κ3 alone 0.53, κ4 alone 0.23-0.26 (almost additive); rank still helps at r3=256/r4=64 (0.859). Using our own C instead of the true one for the modes costs nothing (overlap >= 0.999, also at r=512). D3 is the single most valuable vector (exact D3 alone +0.31 of fraction; g4 +0.04).

### 5.4 Cost ledger of e28fijo (167.55 u = 359.81 GF; 19,867 operations)

| Item | u | share |
|---|---|---|
| Young sources: transport of legs | 42.5 | 25.3 % |
| Young sources: hub D21 contraction | 44.8 | 26.7 % |
| Old level: formation of dense legs | 20.6 | 12.3 % |
| Old level: contraction | 20.4 | 12.2 % |
| Union with the fixed basis | 12.4 | 7.4 % |
| C_pre (W C W^T) | 11.7 | 7.0 % |
| Fine legs | 6.6 | 3.9 % |
| Rest | 8.4 | 5.0 % |

Of the total, matmul at the Strassen leaves is 143.2 u (85 %); Strassen add/sub 9.9 u; copies 2.8 u; QR 3.3 u; einsum 2.5 u. Old level in total 55.6 u (33 %; its own accounting books 22.8 u for legs + basis transport, 2.2 u more than the formation row above); the estimator without it costs 111.9 u. A dense exact (source, layer) pair costs 1.71 u with 5-level Strassen and live-row compaction (3.6-3.9 u without). Fast multiplication is worth -38 % of FLOPs (control without it: x1.62-1.65). Savings that were *exact* and kept: ueye/tri/nest/oldc/fj (-3.3 u, -1.9 %). e30_a vs e28fijo (30 reserved nets): FLOPs -5.9 %, MSE +3.4 %, score x0.973 locally, x0.981 on the server.

### 5.5 Grader facts we paid for

- The residual (Python outside flopscope) is ~6.8 us per billed operation against a 0.4 s limit; the server tail is median + ~0.08 s (our rule: median <= 0.34 s). Submission 333833 (+2,700 operations) lost 18 of 100 nets; 335262 lost all nets (1,024-iteration Python loops per layer). Core clock varies up to x1.25 between server runs and between Kaggle machines.
- **A reference to `numpy` that is never executed (`__import__("numpy").save` in a debug line) gets "Prohibited file in submission" (335913), and `validate-package` does not detect it** - grep before submitting.
- flopscope 0.12.1: matmul bills 2mkn - mn, copies per element, views free, `setup` not billed in u. Our chain is unaffected by the 14 billing fixes reported in the forum.
- Local-to-server transfer. Score predictions written before sending fell inside the interval for 9 of the 13 graded candidates/probes since 03/10 (e8, e9, e10, e14, the level-2-age probe, e20, e24hot, e28fijo, e30_a) and missed four times (e7: +7 %; e13: 18 nets lost to the residual; e17: predicted x0.99, measured x1.0003 - the raw gain x0.951 was eaten by +4.9 % cost; K#9: local gain, server +0.85 % +- 0.36). The server penalises rank cuts ~1.4x the local estimate; MSE gains transferred ~x0.67.

### 5.6 Method lessons (reusable)

1. **Oracles with injected truth need two independent noise halves.** Injected truth carries its Monte-Carlo noise into the output and biases the gain *against* you; with 2^23 samples we produced a false "compensation between layers". Use x_clean = 2x(V) - mean(x(A), x(B)) (valid when x is quadratic in the noise; we checked linearity in the noise variance), and keep truth noise well below the error. The 2x - x_A correction fails when the halves disagree.
2. **Pre-register with a stated hit rate and report the misses.** Examples: server-score intervals 9/13 inside (5.5); "origin of the old D21 error" 2 of 5 mechanism predictions right (the premise was false); oracle A 7 of 10; "newborn hub" 4 of 5. Several hypotheses that looked certain (e.g. an "E1 ceiling x0.77") were measured against a simplified chain and were false against the real estimator (g ~ 0.01).
3. **Oracle -> implementation transfer is not ~1.** Our rule was x_real = 1 - t(1 - x_oracle) with t = 0.5-0.7; in practice the three cheap pieces we implemented (closed-form D21, feed3 x c, mu.mu^T) transferred 0 of 3 (D21: oracle gain 0.108 -> -0.017; feed3 -2..-3 % -> +0.8 %; mu.mu^T -2.7 % -> +1.2 %). Gains measured on a dense GPU route did not transfer to the official route (Strassen + physical removal) either.
4. **Co-adaptation at every level.** A piece better in isolation worsens the total (C1, k3corr, κ4 iiii; with the old level removed, injecting the true σ² alone makes layers 9-12 42 % worse because the table compensated σ² bias with κ3's). Re-fit the cheap tables (leave-one-net-out) after any change, otherwise a result is only a bound: refit moved the slab oracle from x0.374 to x0.224 (not the +-3 % we predicted), moved state-truncation results by x0.3-0.8, and a stale table on a new base worsened 42 %. Equally, after refit the base *without* the piece got worse out of sample (x1.08), so report both.
5. **Alignment, not accuracy.** A local change delta improves the chain only if cos(delta, e) < -‖delta‖/(2‖e‖); error energy is not the metric (directions that matter for the MSE carry little energy: a basis chosen by the error metric gained 1.6-2.1x in error^2 but only ~15-20 % in rank).
6. **At least 4 networks, always.** Three nets said -1 % for a pass count that was -0.07 % +- 0.26 over 13 nets; the per-net sd of an effect is 1.8-3 %; one net gave 0.00 % where 100 gave +2.2 %.
7. **Audit -> decompress -> cheap equivalent.** First locate where the error is born (layer, age, term, structure, type), then ask for the cheapest object that carries it. Several diagnostics reversed a premise we were about to build on (old D21 error 8.7 % -> 4.6 %; "the gap is a rescaling" -> R2 0.10; "S by a scale model" -> R2_K 0.2-0.4).
8. **The server as yardstick.** Paired multi-arm probes (the arm identified from billed FLOPs of marker products) resolved 0.5-1 % effects with SE 0.1-1.4 %; local synthetic nets mispredicted the server twice.
9. **Compute the ceiling against the real estimator before building.** The "E1" ceiling x0.77 became g ~ 0.01; the (3,1) ceiling x0.75 became x0.98 as a bound once measured in the real chain.

### 5.7 What did work (for contrast)

Dead-neuron removal on V29 (4.935e-9 at 0.2265 B); the ridge mean-correction table (-10.4 % on 30 reserved nets, 333693); Strassen/rank-1 pieces (-6.6 % cost, 333752); clock reductions that let those fit (333846); fixed-basis old level (raw -4.5 %, FLOPs -2.8 %, 335690); old level only in non-hot rows (-2.4 % cost at equal MSE, 335727); exact fixed-cost savings (-1.95 % FLOPs, 335741); tau 2.85 + hot 3.0 + tilt -0.1 + R_OLD 416 (-1.9 % score, 335981). All were cost or calibration steps; none changed the κ3/κ4 content.

## 6. Open questions (12; what we know / what we could not find)

| # | Question | What we know (numbers) | What we could not find |
|---|---|---|---|
| Q1 | **How can the κ3/κ4 cross term (hub) be carried in a fixed-size state at <~ 15 u?** | The cross term is 18-19 % of the D21 off-diagonal energy per layer; 81 % is transported cross term, 19 % born (cos 0.03); its projection on rank 256 of C_{l+1} reproduces it (x1.10 with the true X1); the stored span covers only 29-37 % of what the next layer asks; a summed state needs r ~ 400 (x0.85 after refit) and costs only 15-25 u *as a store* | A generator of the projected newborn / of X1 with error^2 <= 6e-4 at <= 1.5 u per object |
| Q2 | **How is the born non-Gaussian hub formed cheaply?** | The first-order formula has cos 0.985 with the truth when S is exact; iij alone costs 73-118 u for -2.2..-2.9 % at c=0.3; the κ4 (2,1,1) vertex is worth 3x the iij; K - K_elliptic (69 % of K) is not a function of anything we carry | A model of K - K_elliptic with R2 >= 0.5, or an equivalent cheap object |
| Q3 | **What is the leaders' sub-110-u state?** (~7 u/layer, 4-6 n x n objects per layer [I]) | With the old level removed we are x28-34; they retain x0.55-0.66 of e16's MSE; our oracles say exact storage/transport buys <= 2 % of their advantage and formation of the hub buys the rest (>= 98 %) [I] | Any object of <~ 15 u that reproduces long κ3 memory |
| Q4 | **Why do leaders accumulate less error with depth?** | all-layers/last 0.393-0.432 (ours 0.390); exponent 1.50-1.72 vs 1.79; one team at 1.50 | Whether a depth-recursive correction (not a final-layer corrector) exists |
| Q5 | **What is in the `setup` FLOPs of three top teams (2.8e10-4.2e11, not billed)?** | Network-independent precomputation is worth <= 0.2 % for us (setup does not see the network); the townhall says offline training with external data is allowed and unbilled [C] | What they compute there; learned corrector or calibration |
| Q6 | **What caused the cluster of 12 teams at 1.76-1.80e-8 on 23-30/09?** | It coincides with the forum thread on the dense κ4 channel vs the scalar law (-8.5 % [C]); the scalar κ4 (2,2) law's R2 falls from 0.998 (layer 1) to 0.045 (layer 15) [C] | The exact change |

## 3. Avenues we closed (111)

Columns: **what it is | measured (nets) | why it fails | would work if**. "Refit" = the cheap calibration tables were re-fitted (leave-one-net-out) after the change. Unless noted, x is final-layer MSE relative to the estimator the piece was tested on, in closed loop (never as an isolated step - see 5.6). The things that *did* work are listed in 5.7.
